HIV-1 Tat induces IL-6 and -8 in astrocytic cell line through NF-κB/AP-1 signaling.

the molecular mechanism involved in the HIV-1 Tat induced IL-6 and 8 in astrocyte cells.
the molecular mechanisms involved in IL-8 production by HIV-1 infected astrocytes, which may be a key factor in the development of HAND.

the identification of the signaling mechanisms involved in the production of inflammatory cytokines by HIV-1 tat in astrocytes, and the results of our studies may be useful in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of HAND.

HIV-1 Tat-induced activation of both NF-kB- and AP-1-mediated transcription of IL-6 in astrocytes is dependent on the activation of both PI3K-Akt and p38δ MAPK, whereas activation of JNK but not of p38 MAPK leads to AP-1 activation and subsequent production of IL-8.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIV-1 Tat-induced IL-6 and -8 production in astrocytes is regulated by NF-κB, and AP-1, where the latter is differentially activated for IL-6 or IL-8.
HIV-1 Tat activates NF-κB via PI3K/AKT and p38 MAP kinase (β subunit), whereas AP-1 is activated by p38δ and JNK MAP kinases for IL-6, and by JNK MAP kinas for IL-8.

the HIV-1 Tat-induced activation of IL-8 is mediated via JNK and p38 MAP kinase, while IL-6 is mediated by p38 MAP kinase and Akt.
